newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank trade hit by lack of funds.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank trade hit by lack of funds.

text.p: Croatian interbank trade was hit by a severe lack of kuna funds on Friday morning but rates were still unchanged, dealers said.
"The money market has had a disastrous morning," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She put demand at 40 million, overshooting the meagre supply of barely 12 million. The central bank was expected to step in with a repo deal to help liquidity.
Supply shrank as banks' clients had to pay weekly turnover tax today and settle monthly benefits.
Fresh loans totalled 12 million kuna, of which 10.5 were call money borrowings at a steady rate of 10.5 percent.
The rest were interbank term loans, granted at 16 percent to a savings bank and at 15 to a commercial bank.

A total of 33.2 million kuna were settled in Thursday's overnight trade as one bank made borrowings to cover its shortfalls and others to maintain their mandatory reserve. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
